report_version.description:
Always `1` for this model. Consumers should refuse versions they do not
know rather than guessing.

run.description: Identity and timing of this run.

outcome.description: Whether the command achieved what it was asked to do.

exit_code.description: The process exit code that accompanies this report.

target.description: The target database, when the command connected to one.

migrations.description: The migrations this command planned or acted on, in execution order.

tests.description: Database test files, in execution order. Empty outside `zapadka test`.

diagnostics.description: Warnings and notes that did not by themselves fail the run.

error.description: Why the run failed. Present if and only if `outcome` is `failure`.

parser_version.description:
The embedded PostgreSQL parser's `PG_VERSION_NUM`, e.g. `180004`.

Recorded because a parser decision — accepting or rejecting a script — is
only reproducible against a specific parser build.

Run.description: Identity and timing of a single run.

id.description:
A UUIDv7 identifying this run. The same id appears on every registry
event the run wrote, so a report can be joined to database history.

started_at.description: When the run started, RFC 3339 in UTC.

finished_at.description: When the run finished, RFC 3339 in UTC.

Outcome.description: Whether a run or step achieved its goal.

oneOf.description: The command did what it was asked to do.
The command did not. `error` explains why.

Target.description:
Facts observed about the target database.

Zapadka records only what it observed or was explicitly given. It never
guesses an operator's identity, hostname, or Git revision.

database.description: The database that was connected to. Never includes credentials.

registry_format_version.description: The registry format version found, before any upgrade this run applied.

lock_timeout.description: The effective `lock_timeout` Zapadka applied, when the target set one.

statement_timeout.description:
The effective `statement_timeout` Zapadka applied, when the target set
one.

MigrationResult.description: What happened to one migration during this run.

slug.description: The human-readable slug from its directory name.

action.description: What the run did, or intended to do, with this migration.

transaction.description: The execution mode the manifest declared.

definition_sha256.description:
SHA-256 of the immutable deployment definition: the canonical manifest
plus `deploy.sql`. This is what history integrity is checked against.

scripts.description: The scripts this action ran, in execution order.

duration_ms.description: Wall-clock duration in milliseconds. Absent for planned-only entries.

error.description: Why this migration failed, when it did.

Action.description: The operation a run performed on a migration.

oneOf.description: Selected for execution but not executed, as in `--dry-run` and `status`.
Applied the migration's `deploy.sql`.
Ran the migration's `verify.sql` against committed state.
Applied the migration's `revert.sql`.
Recorded the migration as applied without running its SQL.

Status.description: The outcome of one migration's action.

oneOf.description: Already applied; the run had nothing to do.
Not applied, and this run did not apply it.
This run applied or verified it successfully.
This run attempted it and it failed.
Selected but deliberately not run, e.g. after an earlier failure.

Applied, but its outcome on the server is unknown and must be resolved
by an operator before deployment can continue.

TransactionMode.description: How a migration's SQL is executed.

oneOf.description: Runs inside a transaction Zapadka opens and closes.
Runs outside any transaction, for statements PostgreSQL forbids in one.

sha256.description:
SHA-256 of the exact bytes executed. Recorded even for mutable scripts
so a past run can be reproduced.

error.description: Why it failed, when it did.

ScriptRole.description: Which of a migration's scripts ran.

oneOf.description: `deploy.sql`, the immutable script that applies the migration.
`revert.sql`, the mutable script that undoes it.
`verify.sql`, the mutable script that checks it, always rolled back.

ReportError.description: A failure, as it appears in a report.

code.description: The stable dotted error code, e.g. `history.definition_changed`.

message.description: One sentence describing what went wrong.

sqlstate.description: PostgreSQL's `SQLSTATE`, when the failure came from the server.

location.description: Where in the project the problem is.

context.description: Additional structured facts, such as expected and actual hashes.

Location.description: A position in a project file.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the file as executed.

status.description: Whether every assertion in the file passed.

assertions.description: Assertions in the order the file emitted them.

planned.description: The plan the file declared, when it declared a count.

error.description: Why the file failed as a whole, e.g. a SQL error or malformed TAP.

Assertion.description: One assertion within a test file.

description.description: The assertion's description, when it gave one.

directive_reason.description: The reason attached to a `TODO` or `SKIP` directive.

diagnostics.description: Diagnostic fields the assertion attached, such as `have` and `want`.

AssertionStatus.description: The result of a single assertion.

oneOf.description: The assertion held.
The assertion did not hold, and it was not marked `TODO`.
Failed, but marked `TODO`, so it does not fail the file.
Passed while marked `TODO`, which usually means the `TODO` is stale.
Not run, because it was marked `SKIP`.

Diagnostic.description: A warning or note that did not by itself fail the run.

code.description:
A stable dotted identifier, e.g. `lint.destructive_drop`. Suppressions
and policy promotion both key on this.

migration_id.description: The migration it concerns, when it concerns one.

location.description: Where in the project it is.

Severity.description: How seriously to take a diagnostic.

oneOf.description: Provably invalid. Always fails the command.
An intentional operational risk. Fails only when policy promotes it.
Informational.
